law.breakBefore: From Dec 10, 2026: when working hours are 4, the break may be skipped if the worker explicitly asks not to take it (new proviso to Labor Standards Act Art. 54(1)).
law.breakAfter: When working hours are 4, the break may be skipped if the worker explicitly asks not to take it (LSA Art. 54(1) proviso, effective Dec 10, 2026). It requires the worker's request; the employer cannot drop it unilaterally. The figure above deducts the legal minimum break.
law.eiBefore: Employment insurance: until Dec 31, 2026 you are covered if you work 60+ hours a month (15+ h/week) or for 3+ consecutive months. From Jan 1, 2027 coverage depends on pay (income) instead of hours; the threshold will be set by Enforcement Decree (reflected once final) (Employment Insurance Act Art. 10, Act No. 21473).
law.eiAfter: Employment insurance: from Jan 1, 2027 you are covered if your pay at that workplace meets the income threshold, regardless of hours. The threshold is set by Enforcement Decree (reflected once final). Daily workers and those employed 3+ consecutive months are covered even below it, and people with two or more jobs can apply to combine pay (Employment Insurance Act Art. 10).

day.title: Daily pay (overtime, night, holiday premiums)
day.desc: Enter start and end times to calculate daily pay at KRW {wage}/h including 50% premiums for overtime (over 8 h), night (22:00–06:00) and holiday work. The legal minimum break (30 min per 4 h, 1 h per 8 h) is deducted automatically.
day.holidayWork: Holiday {hours} h (1.5× up to 8 h, 2× beyond)
day.note: For workplaces with 5+ employees (Labor Standards Act Art. 56). An end time before the start time is treated as the next day.
day.smallNote: Workplaces with fewer than 5 employees are exempt from overtime/night/holiday premiums (Enforcement Decree Annex 1). Weekly holiday pay still applies.

items.a: KRW 10,320 per hour (up 2.9% from KRW 10,030 in 2025). For 40 h/week, the monthly minimum based on 209 hours (incl. 8 h weekly holiday) is KRW 2,156,880, about KRW 25.88 million a year.

items.q: Why divide monthly pay by 209 hours?
items.a: 40 h plus 8 paid holiday hours = 48 h/week; times the average 4.345 weeks per month (365÷7÷12) ≈ 208.6, rounded to 209. For 20 h/week it is (20+4)×4.345 ≈ 104 hours.

items.q: How do I check if my monthly pay violates the minimum wage?
items.a: Switch the input to monthly with holiday pay included and check that the hourly figure is at least that year's minimum (KRW 10,320 in 2026, KRW 10,700 in 2027). Some allowances and bonuses have separate inclusion rules, so the actual judgment may differ.

items.q: When should holiday pay be excluded?
items.a: For workers under 15 h/week, or when comparing contracts that exclude holiday pay. Holiday pay is mandatory at 15+ hours with full attendance, so excluding it overstates the hourly wage.

items.q: Do part-timers get overtime and night premiums?
items.a: At workplaces with 5+ regular employees, yes: +50% for overtime (over 8 h/day or 40 h/week), night work (22:00–06:00) and holiday work (+100% for holiday hours beyond 8). Workplaces under 5 employees are exempt.

conversion.title: Conversion Basis
items: Monthly hours = (weekly hours + holiday hours) × 365÷7÷12 (40 h/week = 209 h)
Holiday hours = weekly hours ÷ 40 × 8 (15+ h/week, max 8)
Monthly = hourly × monthly hours, annual = monthly × 12
Daily = hourly × daily hours (weekly hours ÷ days per week)

tips.title: Notes
items: The same monthly pay gives a different hourly wage depending on holiday pay (40 h/week: 209 h vs 174 h)
Overtime (over 8 h/day or 40 h/week) earns a 50% premium — workplaces with 5+ employees
Night work (22:00–06:00) earns a 50% premium, stacked with overtime (5+ employees)
Holiday work earns 50% up to 8 h and 100% beyond (5+ employees, Labor Standards Act Art. 56)
